statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the maximum of the set of all sums Σ_{i=0}^{len(heights)-1} b[i], where b ranges over all integer sequences of length len(heights) satisfying: (a) 0 <= b[i] <= heights[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights); and (b) b is mountain-shaped, meaning there exists an index p with 0 <= p < len(heights) such that b[0] <= b[1] <= ... <= b[p] and b[p] >= b[p+1] >= ... >= b[len(heights)-1].
preconditions: heights is a non-empty slice of 64-bit integers, len(heights) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), 1 <= heights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail) for every input satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: heights is a non-empty slice of 64-bit integers, len(heights) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), 1 <= heights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r <= Σ_{i=0}^{len(heights)-1} heights[i].
preconditions: heights is a non-empty slice of 64-bit integers, len(heights) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), 1 <= heights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r >= max{ heights[i] | 0 <= i < len(heights) }.
preconditions: heights is a non-empty slice of 64-bit integers, len(heights) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), 1 <= heights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r and r >= len(heights).
preconditions: heights is a non-empty slice of 64-bit integers, len(heights) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), 1 <= heights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every input heights satisfying the preconditions, let r be the result returned on heights and let r_rev be the result returned on the reversed slice rev(heights), where rev(heights)[i] = heights[len(heights)-1-i] for 0 <= i < len(heights). Then both results exist and r = r_rev.
preconditions: heights is a non-empty slice of 64-bit integers, len(heights) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), 1 <= heights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Let r be the result returned on heights and let r' be the result returned on heights'. Then both results exist and r <= r'.
preconditions: heights and heights' are non-empty slices of 64-bit integers with the same length n, n <= 1000, 1 <= heights[i] <= 1000000000 and 1 <= heights'[i] <= 1000000000 for every i with 0 <= i < n, and heights[i] <= heights'[i] for every i with 0 <= i < n.

statement: The function returns a result r, and there exists an integer sequence b of length len(heights) such that (a) 0 <= b[i] <= heights[i] for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), (b) b is mountain-shaped, meaning there exists an index p with 0 <= p < len(heights) such that b[0] <= b[1] <= ... <= b[p] and b[p] >= b[p+1] >= ... >= b[len(heights)-1], and (c) Σ_{i=0}^{len(heights)-1} b[i] = r.
preconditions: heights is a non-empty slice of 64-bit integers, len(heights) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), 1 <= heights[i] <= 1000000000.

preconditions: heights is a non-empty slice of 64-bit integers, len(heights) <= 1000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), 1 <= heights[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: The function returns a result r, and there exist an index p with 0 <= p < len(heights) and an integer sequence b of length len(heights) such that b is mountain-shaped, b[i] <= b[p] for every i with 0 <= i < len(heights), 0 <= b[i] <= heights[i] for every i, b[p] = heights[p], and Σ_{i=0}^{len(heights)-1} b[i] = r.
